findings.title: Destructured destinationCalendar element dereferenced without null check
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendars (array empty or null). The next line accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, so any booking whose location is Google Meet and which has no destination calendar will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, failing the whole create flow. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Organization slug logic inverted (unrelated to PR purpose)
findings.body: The condition was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts behaviour: with team billing enabled the org is now created with a live `slug` *and* `metadata.requestedSlug`, while with billing disabled it gets no slug at all (previously the opposite). This bypasses the paid-slug reservation flow and leaves non-billing instances with slug-less organizations. The change also appears unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor.

findings.title: Dead fallback lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent always returns undefined
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and can never match. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Result: when no externalCalendarId is stored on the reference, `calendarId` is `undefined` for `events.update` (request fails) and falls back to `primary` in `deleteEvent` (wrong calendar). Same pattern at line 317.

findings.title: createEvent called without externalId for credential-less destination calendars
findings.body: In the `else` branch (destination calendar without `credentialId`) `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the third `externalId` argument. Since `referencesToCreate` now takes `externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId` (instead of `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` as before), these bookings will be persisted with `externalCalendarId: undefined`, so later updates/cancellations cannot target the right calendar — a regression for legacy destination calendars that have no credentialId.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and then the collective hosts' calendars are appended with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. Because of the optional chaining, when the value is `null` all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are discarded, so co-hosts get no calendar event — exactly the case this PR aims to fix. Initialise an array instead.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and the no-user guard for dynamic bookings
findings.body: The new dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which the previous version included and which downstream code uses (e.g. for org-aware booker URLs/links). Additionally, there is no check that the queried users actually exist/match `dynamicUserList.length`, so a booking for a non-existent username now proceeds with fewer (or zero) users instead of failing clearly.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation now deletes each event once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring branch (which already loops over all of the user's calendar credentials and all updated bookings) is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references the same delete requests are issued N times, multiplying API calls to the calendar providers and producing repeated 404/410 handling. The recurring handling should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop.

findings.title: updateEvent may be called with undefined credential
findings.body: If `this.calendarCredentials` has no match and the DB lookup returns nothing (or the credential has no `app.slug`), `credential` remains `undefined` but `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still invoked, leading to a runtime failure inside `getCalendar`/`credential.appName` rather than a skipped reference. Guard with `if (credential)` before pushing.

findings.title: Inconsistent destinationCalendar expectations across webhook tests
findings.body: BOOKING_REJECTED now expects `destinationCalendar: []` while BOOKING_CREATED (line 119) and BOOKING_REQUESTED (line 373) still expect `null`. Since `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is now an array type, these payloads are shape-dependent on which code path built the event; the inconsistency makes the contract ambiguous for webhook consumers and leaves the array-with-multiple-hosts case untested.
